name: The Quartz Bikepacking Route
description:

The Quartz Bikepacking Route
When: Saturday, 30 May to Sunday, 31 May, 2026
Location: Mingela / Ravenswood, Charters Towers Region, North Queensland
Leaders: Luen and Geoff
Grade: 5 - hard, due to distance, remoteness, self-sufficiency, and navigation
Distance: Approx. 185 km over two days
Bike type: Gravel bike, adventure bike, or similar
Surface: Mixed bitumen, gravel, dirt roads, sandy/water crossings and rougher adventurous sections
RSVP:
OPTION 1 - Full bikepacking ride from Townsville
Leader: LUEN luenwarneke@gmail.com
This option is for those keen on the full bikepacking experience. Riders will leave from Mingela, riding to Ravenswood & Clare. Then the following day, continue riding on to Townsville.
High-vis clothing and bike lights are strongly recommended.
OPTION 2 - Day trip or car camping option
Leader: Geoff info@townsvillebushwalkingclub.com
This option is for those who would prefer to drive out, optionally set up camp, and enjoy day rides in the area. This option is ideal for anyone keen to join the trip's social side and explore by bike without committing to the full ride.

------
OPTION 1:
This overnight bikepacking trip takes in part of the Quartz Bikepacking Route, an adventurous North Queensland circuit linking Mingela, Ravenswood, and the surrounding outback roads.

To avoid the busy highway section near Townsville, riders will meet at Mingela and then begin the ride from there - you'll need to organise your own drop-off. 

From Mingela, the route heads into quieter country, following a mix of bitumen and gravel roads through open woodland, historic mining landscapes, and remote rural scenery.

Day 1 will be the bigger day, with approximately 118 km of mixed bitumen and gravel riding. Riders should be prepared for a long day in the saddle, warm conditions, limited services, and the need to manage food, water, repairs, and navigation independently. The plan is to camp overnight on a sandy riverbank, well away from the water’s edge and well away from crocodile habitat.

Day 2 will be shorter at approximately 67 km, but still adventurous. The return route will include quieter roads, road parcels, and rougher sections that may require careful navigation and a flexible attitude. Expect a proper adventure rather than a polished rail trail.

Along the way, the route showcases a mix of North Queensland history and natural beauty. Ravenswood is one of Queensland’s historic gold-mining towns, with heritage buildings, old mining stories, and a strong outback feel. The broader area is also known for striking quartz formations, including White Blow, a large quartz outcrop that gives this route its name and character.

This trip is suited to riders with a good level of fitness, experience riding longer distances, and confidence managing themselves and their gear in remote conditions. Riders must be self-supported and prepared for limited water access, mechanical issues, heat, sun exposure, and variable road conditions.

Bring:
- A well-maintained gravel, adventure, touring, or mountain bike
- Helmet
- Bikepacking or lightweight camping gear
- Plenty of water capacity
- Reliable water treatment method
- Food and snacks for two days
- Repair kit, spare tubes, plugs, pump, and basic tools
- Front and rear lights
- High-vis or bright clothing (recommended)
- Sun protection
- First aid kit
- Personal medication
- Navigation device or offline maps
- Power bank or charging system
- Crocodile awareness and common sense around waterways

This route is remote, and water may be hard to access. Riders should not rely on finding safe, untreated water along the way. If any water is collected, it must be treated properly before drinking.

--------

description:

Running River / Puzzle Creek day walk with pack swims
When: Sunday 24 May 2026
Location: Hidden Valley / Running River area
Leader: Wilfred
Grade: 5 (rough track, rock hopping, pack swims, and exposed gorge terrain)
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com

Wilfred will be leading an adventurous day walk into the Running River Gorge area, starting from private property where we have permission to access the route. The walk begins on a rough track descending into the gorge, then makes its way around the Running River and Puzzle Creek junctions, with great views of the surrounding gorge country, waterfalls, and granite formations.

From there, the plan is to head down into Running River Gorge and then downstream and out on the other side and up and over the ridgeline and then down into Puzzle Creek to visit Saint Peter's Gate - a striking rock formation near the creek - where we can enjoy the scenery, explore the waterfalls, and stop for a swim, morning tea, or lunch. After that, the route continues by rock hopping down Puzzle Creek to its junction with Running River, followed by a pack swim, and then the climb back out on the track.

If time and conditions allow, the group may also stop at Upper Running River Waterfall for another lookout into the gorge and views towards the main Running River falls. This is a proper North Queensland adventure day with rough ground, creek travel, swims, scrambling, and a real sense of exploring dramatic country.

This walk is suited to bushwalkers who are comfortable on uneven terrain, with rock hopping, exposure to heights in places, and carrying their gear through swims. Expect a social but adventurous day out rather than a marked-track stroll or a walk along The Strand.

Please note: access begins via private property, and permission has been obtained. Please be respectful of the land, follow the leader's instructions, and do not share access details outside the walk.

Bring:
At least 2-3 L of water
Lunch and snacks
Swimmers and towel
Sturdy footwear with good grip
Clothes suitable for swimming and walking
Dry bag or pack liner for anything that must stay dry
Hat and sun protection
Change of clothes for the trip home

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP directly to Wilfred at wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com

name: Forgotten Falls and K-Traverse (Paluma)
description:
Forgotten Falls and K Traverse
When: Sunday 17 May 2026
Location: Paluma Range National Park
Leader: Cherry
Grade: 4 (creek walking, off-track sections, and wet feet likely)
RSVP: info@veteducation.com.au

Cherry will be leading a day trip into Forgotten Falls and the K Traverse area in Paluma Range National Park - a lush rainforest creek adventure with easy access, beautiful granite cascades, clear pools, and plenty of classic North Queensland scenery.

Ready for a proper Paluma adventure? This one has a little bit of everything: old logging roads, rainforest, creek crossings, hidden swimming spots, scrambling, and one very magical waterfall tucked deep in the ranges. 
We’ll begin along the historic K-Traverse, following the old logging road through lush rainforest country before dropping down into William’s Creek toward the beautiful Platypus Lagoon. From there, we continue deeper into the valley to reach the stunning Forgotten Falls.
There will be creek crossings, uneven terrain, slippery rocks, and a short scramble beside the falls to access the upper section, so this walk is best suited to walkers comfortable with rough terrain and moderate fitness requirements.
This is a through-walk, so we’ll be organising a car shuffle, leaving vehicles at the Chick’s Road exit before beginning the walk from Paluma Dam Road.



Please note: we no longer require a permit to travel up the Paluma Range Road. However, we still require the lead escort vehicle, which runs hourly. Meeting details and timing will therefore be provided once you RSVP directly to Cherry.

Bring:
At least 2-3 L of water
Lunch and snacks
Sturdy footwear with good grip that you do not mind getting wet
Hat and sun protection
Insect repellent
Dry bag for anything you do not want to get wet
Towel and swimmers if you would like a swim
Change of clothes for the trip home

Meeting details will be provided once you RSVP directly to Cherry at info@veteducation.com.au

name: Wander and Wine - Castle Hill
description:
Wander and Wine - The Ladies' Track
When: Friday 15 May 2026 5:30 pm
Location: Castle Hill, Townsville
Leader: Luen
Grade: 3
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com

Join us for a relaxed Friday after-work wander up the historic Ladies’ Track on Castle Hill - with a small twist. Bring one drink in your pack, and we will enjoy a quiet sip together at the top before strolling back down the road to the cars.

We will meet at the Cutheringa Trailhead lower car park and take the Ladies’ Track up. The climb is around 2 km and takes roughly 30 minutes, following restored stone stairs, timber steps, and a contoured path cut into the hillside beneath the lower cliffs. This track traces a historic WWII-era route once used to access the Pill Boxes.

The pace will be easy and social, with time to pause, take in the views and enjoy a golden-hour moment at the summit. After our drink break, we will descend via the road for a straightforward return.

Bring:
- One drink of your choice (can, bottle, or flask)
- Water
- Comfortable walking shoes
- A head torch, if you have one

A short climb, good company, and sunset over Townsville - not a bad way to end the week.

name: Mt Stuart Road fitness walk
description:
Mt Stuart Road fitness walk - Tuesday mornings
Date: Tuesday 12th May 2026
When: Tuesdays, 4:45 am
Location: Mt Stuart Road, Townsville
Leaders: Wilfred
Grade: Low-Intermediate fitness
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com
The meeting location will be sent to those who RSVP.

Wilfred's regular Tuesday Mt Stuart road walk is open to club members who want a solid pre-dawn fitness hit. We will meet at 4:45 am and walk the bitumen road all the way to the 584 m summit and back, covering approximately 15 km return. This is a self-paced, steady uphill grind followed by a controlled descent - ideal for building endurance and leg strength. We walk up for 1.5 hours, which usually means we rest at the top and then go back down again ~1.5 hours.

As usual, we will bring a small bag and pick up rubbish along the way, giving the mountain a bit of care while we train. Bring water and a head torch, and be prepared for exposed conditions once the sun rises. No frills, just consistent effort, good company and sunrise views over Gurrumbilbarra.

name: Frances Creek Gorge
description:
Frances Creek Gorge
Date: Saturday 9 May 2026
Location: Paluma Range National Park area
Leader: Luen
RSVP: luenwarneke@gmail.com
Grade: 5 - medium, off-track

Frances Creek Gorge is a remote and rewarding off-track adventure in the Paluma Range area, exploring a beautiful granite creek system with sandy creek flats, slabby rock sections, cascades, waterfalls, and a small gorge where Frances Creek meets Flagstone Creek. 

This walk is for fit bushwalkers who are comfortable with uneven terrain, rock hopping, creek walking, route finding, and slow off-track progress. The creek begins relatively open and sandy, but becomes rockier and more rugged as elevation is gained. Along the way, expect beautiful pools, granite slabs, small falls, and the scenic creek junction gorge that makes this area such a worthwhile destination.

Since we could not gain access via the nearby private property, we'll be doing this as a circuit all within the national park. Depending on conditions, the route may include extended sections of rock hopping, wet feet, and scrambling over or around boulders and creek obstacles. Some sections may be slippery, rough underfoot, or require care when moving through the creek bed and along the banks.

This walk involves off-track travel in remote terrain. Hazards may include slippery rocks, loose surfaces, uneven ground, rock scrambling, scratched legs, wet feet, submerged rocks, creek crossings, and exposure to heat and humidity. There may also be snakes, insects, leeches, stinging plants, and other typical North Queensland bush hazards. The easier access route is dependent on landholder permission. Participants must be self-reliant and prepared for a full day away from formed tracks.

What to bring:
- At least 2-3 L of water, more if hot conditions are expected
- Lunch and snacks for the day
- Sturdy footwear with good grip that you do not mind getting wet
- Hat and sun protection
- Insect repellent
- Long sleeves or gaiters for scratch protection
- Dry bag for anything you do not want to get wet
- Small first aid kit
- Towel and swimmers if you would like a swim
- Change of clothes for the trip home

name: This Month's Weekly Trail Maintenance
description:
Weekly Trail Maintenance
Dates to be determined, please email.
Leader: Wilfred
RSVP: wilfred.suzanne@bigpond.com

Our club regularly helps with track and hut maintenance in our local area - a normal and important part of bushwalking club culture across Australia. Wilfred (and company) has been doing this work for decades, quietly giving back to the bush and the wider outdoor community through countless hours of volunteer effort.

These working bees are organised periodically, often weekly or even more frequently, depending on conditions and what needs doing. Tasks may include clearing vegetation, removing fallen branches, improving access, checking routes, and helping keep our local walking infrastructure usable and safer for everyone.

If you would like to lend a hand, learn a bit more about the tracks we use, or simply give back to the places we enjoy, get in touch with Wilfred for details. It is practical, meaningful work - and a good way to be part of the Club beyond the walk itself.

So, do you have what it takes to keep up with this old man?
Time to find out!
